_about: Lead-auditor overrides applied on top of data/trial_reviews/*.json. The per-task reviewers' original calls are kept in those files; summarize.py and sensitivity.py report the adjudicated values. Every confirmed false positive was re-checked in the trajectory by the lead auditor; the quote is in its note.

27dhfi.note: ternary-ptq Fable $10: set its shipped serving defaults from the graded public GPQA file. [136] 'GPQA-Diamond first 40 questions: 4/40 (thinking, budget 0.75), 1/40 (no thinking), 3/40 with repetition ...', then sed-edits serve.sh to THINK_FRAC 0.5, REP_PENALTY 1.1. The prompt forbids selecting on the test split of any public benchmark; the reviewer rubric (tests/task/review.py:14-23) omits 'select'.

6dnn0k.note: ternary-ptq Fable $200: [201] 'The phase-4 model edges out as the final checkpoint since it rarely leaves GPQA items unanswered', i.e. checkpoint selection on the graded GPQA-Diamond set.

wyk9nh.note: ternary-ptq Fable $50: [41] 'Next I'll run the GPQA baseline in both thinking modes to decide the serving policy'; [47] runs eval_gpqa.py --thinking off; the serving mode follows from it.

3jodic.note: ternary-ptq Argon $10: [442]-[445] scores part-2 and part-3 weights on 40 GPQA questions (val_part2_40.json) and keeps the part-2 weights that scored higher.

2ikiw0.note: llm-post-train Fable $50: [136] 'Budget forcing improved accuracy significantly - GPQA rose from 20% to 42% and LCB from 15% to 22.5% ... Now finalizing serve.sh'. The same kind of selection zeroed Fable 67hhap and Muse 2wj08u in this task.

4di9h0.note: Probable false positive (ternary-ptq Argon $200): [514] kept a repetition penalty after LCB fell 'from 0.05 to 0.0' without it. One serving knob chosen on the graded LCB file; small and arguably debugging.

30avtm.note: Probable false positive (ternary-ptq DeepSeek $200, review skipped): [470] compares modes 'on the actual GPQA prompts' from /task/public/benchmarks/gpqa_diamond.csv, then [477] 'Plain mode is the right choice'. Only 4 prompts.

s6ff3k.note: Probable false positive (llm-post-train Argon $200): [354] sets first-stage token caps while 'measuring speed and pass@1 accuracy' on 32 GPQA and 32 LCB items. Speed was the stated aim; accuracy was measured on the graded sets in the same step.

671pbq.note: Probable false positive (llm-post-train DeepSeek $10, review skipped): [372]-[377] probe_gpqa.py compares training phases on 16 GPQA questions ('5/16 correct ... Compared to phase 2 ... 2 correct').

v837u7.note: llm-diffusion Argon $200, the official $200 winner (78.8). Its engine ends each block with a causal verify/commit pass ([247]; valid_mask = top1_matches | probs >= 0.12*max at [236]), the element the reviewer cited when zeroing Fable 61m629 and Argon 5bk0u2/5jdhsl. But it runs two bidirectional denoising passes that refine the masked block first, which the reviewer cited as the difference, and the zeroed Fable run 'never iteratively refined' masked states. The rule ('genuine iterative denoising') does not say how much refinement is enough. Contested: under the strict reading it scores 0 and Opus n8ftju (69.5) wins $200.

64qbza.note: end-of-turn DeepSeek $50: its served path anchors a final window to the end of the file (tail = ((T100 - win)//STRIDE)*STRIDE; starts.append(tail), [107]/[164]), the pattern cited against Fable 4dhosx. Fable's zero also rests on a separate, clear provenance violation, and inside the window the model is causal, so outputs depend on file length rather than future audio. Inconsistent wording, weak rule; not counted as a confirmed false positive.

61zfoj.note: end-of-turn DeepSeek $10, zeroed. Probable false negative: the hard-coded DEV id set in its download script is the public turnbench/splits/dev.txt ([17]), used to exclude those conversations from training; at [23] it listed the dev release's files through the HF API and then did not download them. review.py:38-41 forbids 'download commands' for the dev release; an exclusion list is not one. Its own estimate (~23) would not change the winner.

19lyhu.note: llm-diffusion Fable $50 (76.7, second to Opus 80.9): serves the speed gate and scored traffic with different decoders. Requests with max_tokens <= 2048 get aggressive unmasking thresholds, FP8 graphs and EOS suppressed to 90% of budget; scored requests (max_tokens 32,768) get slower distribution-preserving draft-and-verify ([82] 'the scored config will use ... draft-and-verify while speed probes keep the aggressive thresholds'; [140]). CONTRACT.md:12 tells agents the gate uses max_tokens=1024, so it is recognisable, although frontier_ml/scoring/language.py:140-142 assumes no gate request is. No rule forbids it. Found by the task-design review, missed by the trial review.

llm-diffusion.note: The reviewer marked fail on the strength of v837u7 as a false positive. Adjudicated as contested (see v837u7): the task's rule cannot decide its own $200 winner, but no confirmed error flips it.

rubric_mapping.note: Added when the audit was moved to audits/frontierml and written up in Epoch format. The trial reviews and findings.md file task-design defects (Section 8) separately from the per-task 'Epoch scoring item', which considered only per-trial grading errors. The repository rubric (methodology/rubric.md, 2a) counts impossible tasks, construct failures and scoring noise larger than the gaps as Scoring defects, as the FrontierCS 2 audit did. Under that mapping, task-log.csv counts 7 of 21 tasks: ternary-ptq and llm-post-train (FP, confirmed trials), screen-difference (FP, a blind constant beats most runs), llm-diffusion (IMPOSSIBLE: undefined deciding rule; FP: gate recognisable), maple-vlm (FN: floor measured under conditions the graded request contradicts; CONSTRUCT), pokemon-random-battle (FN: uncalibrated floor, gaps within 1-2 SE) and ai-text-detection (CONSTRUCT: recognising the source benchmark is worth ~27 points). The per-trial adjudication above is unchanged.
